title: Rush
why: Niki Lauda's Ferrari catches fire at Bergwerk on the second lap of the German Grand Prix, 1 August 1976.
alt: Warsaw 44 — the Uprising begins at 5pm, 1 August 1944

title: Race
why: Jesse Owens wins the Olympic 100 metres in Berlin on 3 August 1936, in front of Hitler.
alt: Columbus sails from Palos, 3 August 1492 — 1492: Conquest of Paradise

title: The Diary of Anne Frank
why: The Gestapo climb the stairs behind the bookcase on the morning of 4 August 1944.
alt: Anne Frank Remembered (1995); Britain declares war, 4 August 1914 — Oh! What a Lovely War

title: The 33
why: The San José mine collapses on 5 August 2010 with thirty-three men 700 metres down.
alt: Marilyn Monroe found dead, 5 August 1962 — Blonde; My Week with Marilyn

title: Barefoot Gen
why: 8:15am, 6 August 1945, Hiroshima — animated with a child's-eye literalism no live action has matched.
alt: Hiroshima Mon Amour; Black Rain (1989)

title: Man on Wire
why: Philippe Petit steps out on a wire between the Twin Towers at 7:15am on 7 August 1974 and stays there for 45 minutes.
alt: The Walk (2015)

title: Once Upon a Time in Hollywood
why: The final chapter opens on a card: Saturday, August 8th, 1969 — and then rewrites what happened on Cielo Drive.
alt: Nixon — the resignation speech, 8 August 1974

title: La Marseillaise
why: Renoir's Marseillais federes march north and storm the Tuileries on 10 August 1792.
alt: Danton

title: Kursk
why: The Kursk's torpedo explodes on 12 August 2000 and twenty-three men wait in compartment nine.
alt: The Perfect Storm

title: The Tunnel
why: The wire goes up across Berlin overnight on 13 August 1961, and the digging starts.
alt: One, Two, Three (1961); Bridge of Spies

title: Belfast
why: Opens on 15 August 1969, the afternoon the street Buddy lives on is torn apart.
alt: Woodstock begins 15 August 1969; VJ Day; Viceroy's House — Indian independence, 15 August 1947

title: Peterloo
why: The yeomanry ride into 60,000 people at St Peter's Field, Manchester, 16 August 1819.
alt: Elvis — Presley dies at Graceland, 16 August 1977

title: Woodstock
why: Three days on Max Yasgur's farm, 15–18 August 1969; the 17th is the day it stops raining and turns into a nation.
alt: Taking Woodstock (2009)

title: Iron Jawed Angels
why: The Nineteenth Amendment is ratified on 18 August 1920 by one vote in Tennessee.
alt: Hendrix closes Woodstock on the morning of 18 August 1969

title: The Unbearable Lightness of Being
why: Warsaw Pact tanks roll into Prague on 21 August 1968 — the invasion begins the night of the 20th and the film cuts real footage into it.
alt: The Prague Spring documentaries

title: Dog Day Afternoon
why: Sonny Wortzik's fourteen-hour bank siege in Gravesend, Brooklyn, 22 August 1972. Attica! Attica!
alt: Michael Collins — killed at Béal na Bláth, 22 August 1922; Richard III — Bosworth Field, 22 August 1485

title: Braveheart
why: William Wallace is hanged, drawn and quartered at Smithfield on 23 August 1305.
alt: Sacco and Vanzetti executed, 23 August 1927

title: Pompeii
why: Vesuvius buries Pompeii on 24 August AD 79 (the traditional date).
alt: The Last Days of Pompeii (1935); Washington burned, 24 August 1814

title: The Day of the Jackal
why: The Jackal picks Liberation Day, 25 August, for his shot at de Gaulle — because that is the one day the General will not duck.
alt: Is Paris Burning? — Paris liberated, 25 August 1944

title: Krakatoa, East of Java
why: Krakatoa detonates on 27 August 1883 and is heard 3,000 miles away. (It was west of Java.)
alt: Mountbatten killed at Mullaghmore, 27 August 1979

title: The Trial of the Chicago 7
why: Everything turns on the night of 28 August 1968 in Grant Park — 'the whole world is watching'.
alt: Till — Emmett Till murdered, 28 August 1955; the March on Washington, 28 August 1963

title: Terminator 2: Judgment Day
why: Skynet becomes self-aware at 2:14am Eastern on 29 August 1997 and fires on Russia.
alt: Katrina makes landfall, 29 August 2005 — Trouble the Water

title: The Queen
why: Diana dies in the Pont de l'Alma tunnel in the early hours of 31 August 1997; the film is the week that follows.
alt: Spencer (2021); Diana (2013)
